slot.brief: Propose a two-step conversion of an alcohol/alkene to an ether via Williamson synthesis with correct alkyl halide choice.

stem: Which sequence converts propene into methyl propan-2-yl ether by Williamson synthesis?
options: (i) BH₃·THF, then H₂O₂/OH⁻; (ii) Na, then CH₃I
(i) BH₃·THF, then H₂O₂/OH⁻; (ii) Na, then C₂H₅Br

verdicts.working: Acid-catalyzed hydration of propene gives propan-2-ol. Treating it with Na forms propan-2-oxide, which reacts with CH₃I to give methyl propan-2-yl ether by Williamson synthesis.

working:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}/\text{H}^+} \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{CH}_3\text{CH(ONa)CH}_3 + \text{H}_2$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(ONa)CH}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{I} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OCH}_3\text{)CH}_3 + \text{NaI}$$
